commitResults.messageTitle: Apply Java coding standards across Athena
commitResults.messageBody:
Rename classes, methods, fields, and constants for clearer intent.

Align production code and unit tests with Java style conventions without intentionally changing application behavior.

Build the current JAR and run UI cases in isolated directories with fail-fast output comparison. Expand the test plan, record the passing session, and document the required verification process.

Add visual diff tooling to support reviewing future changes.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/athena/parser/CommandHandler.java
Simplify find-result numbering and clarify the mark/unmark helper documentation without changing behavior.
Cover command parsing, task models, storage, UI output, date parsing, and the application entry point with success and failure cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor Java code to meet coding standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Several classes use vague identifiers, incomplete documentation, and
less precise types. Their responsibilities are therefore harder to
follow.

- Rename fields and APIs to communicate their roles more clearly.
- Use final fields, primitive booleans, and parameterized collections.
- Align Javadocs, imports, comments, and test names with Java
  conventions.

Preserve application behavior while improving type safety and
maintainability.

Java work lacks a single agent-readable checklist. This can lead to
inconsistent style decisions across source and tests.

Add a project skill that captures naming, layout, structure, and
documentation rules. Require agents to invoke it for Java changes and
reviews so the same standards are applied consistently.

Commit and branch guidance lacks an explicit validation workflow. This
can make repository history inconsistent across agents.

Add a project skill that codifies SE-EDU commit-message and branch-name
rules. Require agents to invoke it when creating or reviewing Git
metadata so repository history remains consistent.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle empty and case-insensitive search in find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Case-sensitive matching can omit relevant tasks, while a blank keyword
unintentionally matches the entire task list.

Ignore capitalization during matching and guide users who omit the
keyword. Add unit and UI tests to prevent regressions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix coding style using peer review
Fix title in README to Athena
Fix Ui Tests to reflect JavaFX changes
Fix issues raised in PR review
Add assertions for invalid program states
commitResults.messageBody:
Core methods rely on invariants that are not enforced, so violations can
surface far from their cause or silently use fallback behavior.

Add assertions to:

- require continuing commands to produce a response
- reject null task collections and null tasks
- ensure every known command has an explicit switch branch

Use assertions because these conditions are programmer invariants rather
than recoverable user errors.

The new assertion formatting violates the project's whitespace and
operator-wrapping rules, causing `checkstyleMain` to fail.

Align the assertions with the configured Checkstyle rules so the code
uses the project's consistent style and passes automated checks.
Add assertions for invalid program states

The traditional switch syntax makes `handleCommand` verbose and harder
to scan because each case requires a separate `break`.

Convert the switch to arrow cases to reduce boilerplate while
preserving the command-handling behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Separate task parsing from loading
commitResults.messageBody:
areItemsLoaded mixes file-loading orchestration with the details of
deserializing each saved task. This makes the method harder to scan and
forces readers to switch abstraction levels inside the loop.

Extract saved-line parsing into a dedicated helper. Keep the loading
method focused on reading records and adding parsed tasks, while
preserving the existing formats and error behavior.

areItemsLoaded sounds like a side-effect-free boolean query, but calling
it reads from disk and populates the supplied task list. This mismatch
obscures the method's responsibility and can surprise callers.

Rename the operation to loadTasks and update its callers, test stub, and
test names. Make the side effect explicit without changing its return
value or loading behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task loading from its status query
commitResults.messageBody:
`loadTasks` changes the supplied task list, so its name should describe
the operation. Its boolean return value conflicts with the naming
convention for boolean methods.

Make `loadTasks` return `void` and expose its outcome through
`wasLoadSuccessful`. This separates the operation from its status query
while giving each method a name that reflects its responsibility.

parseTask uses bare numbers to identify record sizes and field positions.
Readers must reconstruct the save-file schema to understand each task
constructor, and future format changes are easy to apply inconsistently.

Replace those literals with SAVE-prefixed constants and align constructor
arguments with their named fields. Keep the serialized format and parsing
behavior unchanged while making the schema explicit at each use site.

Task uses the literals 1 and 0 independently when saving and loading
completion state. Their meaning is implicit, and duplicated tokens can
drift apart when the storage format changes.

Introduce SAVE_STATUS_DONE and SAVE_STATUS_NOT_DONE as the shared
vocabulary for both directions. Preserve the existing file format and
invalid-status behavior while making each value's purpose explicit.

getStoreStatusIcon sounds like a second display-oriented status icon,
but it returns the numeric token written to storage. Its similarity to
getStatusIcon makes the two representations easy to confuse.

Rename the method to getSaveStatus and update its documentation and tests.
Make the persistence boundary explicit while preserving every serialized
value and public behavior.

DateParser defines the accepted input pattern separately when creating
its formatter and when explaining validation failures. The duplicated
literal can drift, leaving users with guidance that parsing does not
accept.

Introduce a named input pattern and a shared formatter derived from it.
Build the existing error message from the same pattern so the parser and
its guidance stay synchronized without changing accepted input or output.

commitResults.messageTitle: DateParser: Derive sample input from pattern
commitResults.messageBody:
The validation message contains a hard-coded sample date that can
drift from `INPUT_PATTERN` when the accepted format changes.

Generate the sample using `INPUT_PATTERN` so the example remains
consistent with the parser's accepted format.

DateParser exposes a public constructor even though it has no instance
state and every operation is static. This suggests an unsupported
object-oriented usage and adds a meaningless API surface.

Make the constructor private and document that it exists only to prevent
instantiation. Preserve the complete static parsing and formatting API
used by the application.

writeItems uses generic terminology even though the method accepts only
tasks and serializes the complete task list. The name obscures the
domain operation and is inconsistent with loadTasks.

Rename the method to saveTasks and use task-specific parameter, loop, and
test names throughout its call sites. Preserve the existing overwrite
semantics and serialized output.

createAndAddTask delegates one UI call to handleTaskCommand, which has
no reuse or distinct abstraction. Its generic name makes readers jump
to another method to learn what happens after a task is added.

Inline the task-added response at its only call site and remove the
redundant helper. Keep the command flow and user-visible behavior
unchanged while making the creation sequence explicit.

Event's command constructor overwrites its input parameter twice while
removing the /from and /to markers. Reusing the parameter hides the
original command text and makes the parsing data flow harder to follow.

Create one normalizedInput value from the transformations and split
that value into fields. Preserve the parsing sequence and all
user-visible behavior while keeping each variable's purpose stable.

Deadline's command constructor overwrites its input parameter before
splitting the command fields. Reusing the parameter hides the original
text and makes the parsing data flow harder to follow.

Create a separate normalizedInput value for the delimiter replacement
and split that value into fields. Preserve validation and user-visible
behavior while keeping each variable's purpose stable.

handleCommand overwrites its inputLine parameter with a trimmed value
before tokenizing the command. Reusing the parameter conceals the
original input and makes the transformation less explicit.

Introduce a named trimmedInput value and tokenize that value instead.
Preserve command recognition and dispatch behavior while giving each
variable one stable purpose.

GUI uses AthenaException as a normal 'bye' signal. A normal exit is
not an error and should not require an exception.

Return the GUI message and 'bye' signal together via `CommandResponse`.

Both Todo constructors repeat the same empty-description check and
user-facing exception. Keeping two copies allows their validation and
messages to drift when either construction path changes.

Delegate the convenience constructor to the full constructor. Preserve
the incomplete default and existing error message while maintaining one
validation path.

Storage exposes an append-only write method that Athena never calls.
Its only callers are tests dedicated to that unused behavior, so the
method and its tests increase the public surface without protecting an
application requirement.

Remove the dead method, its unused import, and its dedicated tests.
Retain the overwrite-based persistence path used by task saving and
loading.

Task exposes setDone(boolean) even though production code changes status
only through markDone and unmarkDone. The boolean API permits less
expressive calls and adds a one-line indirection to both domain
operations.

Remove setDone and assign the private state inside the two explicit
operations. Remove only the setter-specific test because the retained
tests cover both transitions through the supported API.

Storage infers a task subtype only from the number of saved fields and
ignores the explicit type marker. A corrupted record with a valid field
count can therefore be restored as the wrong task type instead of being
rejected.

Require each supported type marker to match its expected field count.
Reject unknown markers as corrupted data and cover the previously
accepted case with a regression test.

Storage treats every read error as an empty file. This makes an
unreadable or invalid path indistinguishable from a missing data file
and can mislead callers into continuing without persisted tasks.

Handle only a confirmed missing path as empty. Report other read
failures as an AthenaException and cover the distinction with a
regression test.

StorageStub exposes a misspelled wasloadFailed method that has no
callers and performs no action. Its presence suggests the stub can model
failed loading even though wasLoadSuccessful always returns true.

Remove the dead hook so the stub's public surface reflects its supported
behavior and no longer distracts readers with a false capability.

commitResults.messageTitle: DialogBox: Fail fast on layout errors
commitResults.messageBody:
DialogBox logs an FXML loading failure and then continues using fields
that the failed load should initialize. This replaces the root cause
with a later null dereference and leaves construction in an invalid
state.

Throw a contextual IllegalStateException immediately and retain the
IOException as its cause. Keep the successful construction path
unchanged while making failures direct and diagnosable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Main: Fail fast on layout errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Main prints an FXML loading failure and quietly returns from startup.
This suppresses a fatal initialization error and leaves callers without
a clear signal that the window could not be created.

Throw a contextual IllegalStateException and retain the IOException as
its cause. Keep the successful startup path unchanged while making
failures direct and diagnosable.

The Task field and constructor parameters use `name`, while their
Javadocs describe the value as a task description. The validation error
also exposes the less precise term to users.

Rename the identifiers to `description`, update the validation message,
and verify the revised message in tests. Use `description` consistently
because it states the value's role more precisely.

Mark and delete catch IndexOutOfBoundsException across parsing, task
access, UI output, and persistence. An unrelated bounds defect in later
operations can therefore be mistaken for invalid user input.

Limit exception handling to numeric parsing and reject out-of-range
indexes with guard clauses. Keep task mutation and persistence on the
unexceptional path so unexpected defects remain visible.

TaskList exposes its mutable backing list through getTasks. Callers can therefore add, remove, or clear tasks without using the wrapper's operations, and storage loading depends on that encapsulation leak.

Return an immutable snapshot from getTasks and make loading produce a task collection used to construct TaskList. Copy initial tasks so the wrapper remains the sole owner of its collection.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Parse dated commands by delimiter
commitResults.messageBody:
Dated task constructors rewrite command text with regular expressions and then split on every slash. That hides the command grammar and causes ordinary slashes in task descriptions to be parsed as field separators.

Locate the named /by, /from, and /to delimiters directly. Preserve all other slashes as description text and cover that behavior with focused regression tests.
Branch a code quality

Manual loops obscure the intent of command lookup, task filtering, and
task serialization. Replace them with stream pipelines that express these
operations directly and avoid repeated string concatenation.

Parse every saved task before updating the destination list so malformed
data cannot leave partially loaded state. Accept platform-independent line
endings when reading saved tasks.
Refactor task processing with streams

Tasks need lightweight labels for organization and exact multi-tag
searches. Add case-insensitive tags with stable display spelling, CLI
commands to manage and query them, and backward-compatible persistence.

Cover validation, no-op storage behavior, mixed legacy records, and the
end-to-end command flows while documenting the supported tag syntax.
